title: Qwen3.8-27B as Ternary Bonsai 2 (5.95-7.2 GB) on PrismML's llama.cpp
slug_note: PrismML retrained Qwen3.8-27B to ternary weights: the whole 27B in about 6-7 GB, 262K context on a 12 GB card.

variation.quant_detail: Ternary {-1,0,+1} weights. PTQ1_0 packing 1.75 bits/weight (5.95 GB); PQ2_0 2.13 bits/weight (7.21 GB). Card: 98.2% of FP16 benchmark average retained.

engine.config: PrismML llama.cpp fork (ternary hybrid-attention kernels). Stock llama.cpp rejects PTQ1_0/PQ2_0.

fork_revision.locator: card: 'These files need our llama.cpp build'
fork_revision.note: The card states stock llama.cpp rejects PTQ1_0/PQ2_0 as unknown types.

kernel_patches.purpose: Ternary hybrid-attention kernels for Bonsai's {-1,0,+1} weights

requirements.notes: RTX 3060 12 GB report (PTQ1_0, q4 KV cache, flash attention): 7.3 GB resident at a 64K window, 11.7 GB at the full 262K window. The demo downloads PQ2_0 plus the vision projector (7.8 GB).

steps.text: Open http://localhost:8080. setup.sh fetches PrismML's llama.cpp binaries and the PQ2_0 weights (7.8 GB with the vision projector); set BONSAI_OPENWEBUI=0 and BONSAI_CODE_INTERPRETER=0 to skip the extras.
The 12 GB report used the smaller PTQ1_0 file (5.95 GB) to fit the full 262K window; PrismML's card says PTQ1_0 also decodes faster on Ada cards (RTX 4090).

caveats: Not stock llama.cpp: the files need PrismML's fork. Stock llama.cpp rejects PTQ1_0/PQ2_0 and loads Q2_0 silently as garbage (per the card).
m001-m003 are one builder's RTX 3060 12 GB report (PTQ1_0, prebuilt CUDA 12.4 fork binary, full 262K window, q4 KV). m004-m005 are PrismML's own llama-bench table.
Quality figures (83.9 vs 85.4 for Qwen3.8-27B, 98.2% retained) are PrismML's own 20-benchmark suite, not independently reproduced.
Thinking is on by default at xhigh effort; give a large output limit (the card suggests -n 16384).
